title: applyFilterExpression uses eval() with no tests
why: The function passes a caller-supplied string directly to eval(). Without tests, there is no verification that arbitrary code execution is blocked, that malicious expressions are rejected, that the return type is correct for valid predicates, or that exceptions surface predictably. Any attacker reaching POST /notes/filter can run arbitrary Python in the server process.
evidence:
def applyFilterExpression(notes, expression):
    return [n for n in notes if eval(expression)]
fix: test_applyFilterExpression_arbitrary_code_execution — pass an expression like '__import__("os").getenv("HOME")' and assert it raises an exception or is refused; also test_applyFilterExpression_valid_expression with a safe predicate and known note list to assert correct filtering.

title: current_user_id has no tests — token parsing is trivially bypassable
why: The function trusts whatever integer follows the last '.' in the token string without verifying the signature. Without tests, there is no assertion that a crafted token like 'anything.999' is rejected, that None is returned for missing/malformed tokens, or that an attacker cannot impersonate any user by fabricating the trailing segment.
fix: test_current_user_id_forged_token — call current_user_id('forged.42') and assert it does NOT return 42 (i.e., assert signature verification is enforced); test_current_user_id_missing_token — call with None and assert returns None; test_current_user_id_malformed_token — call with 'noperiod' and assert returns None.

title: isAdmin has no tests — static bypass token goes unvalidated
why: Admin gate is a single string equality check against a hardcoded token ('letmein-admin'). Without tests, there is no assertion that the gate correctly rejects missing, empty, or wrong tokens, that case sensitivity is enforced, or that the 204 delete path is unreachable without the correct credential. A test would also document the expected bypass-token rotation mechanism (currently none).
fix: test_isAdmin_correct_token — call isAdmin({'X-Admin-Token': 'letmein-admin'}) and assert True; test_isAdmin_wrong_token — call with a wrong value and assert False; test_isAdmin_missing_header — call with empty dict and assert False.

title: issue_token has no tests — token format and signature correctness unverified
why: The function builds a token from user_id, timestamp, and JWT_SECRET using SHA-1, then appends user_id in plaintext. Without tests there is no assertion that the produced token has the expected format, that current_user_id can round-trip it, or that changing JWT_SECRET produces a different hash (i.e., the HMAC-like scheme is actually keyed). Bugs here would silently break all authenticated endpoints.
fix: test_issue_token_format — call issue_token(7) and assert the result matches r'^[0-9a-f]{40}\.7$'; test_issue_token_roundtrip — assert current_user_id(issue_token(7)) == 7; test_issue_token_secret_sensitivity — assert issue_token(7) with one secret differs from a token produced with a different secret.

title: search_notes changed to f-string interpolation — SQL injection path untested
why: The PR replaced parameterised query placeholders with direct f-string interpolation of both user_id and query. Without tests, there is no verification that a crafted query like q="' OR '1'='1" or user_id=None produces an error rather than leaking all rows. Previously a test would have passed with the safe parameterised version; no equivalent test now guards the new unsafe form.
evidence:
sql = f"SELECT id, title, body FROM notes WHERE user_id = {user_id} AND title LIKE '%{query}%'"
cur.execute(sql)
fix: test_search_notes_sql_injection — call search_notes("' OR '1'='1", 1) against a test DB and assert it returns only rows belonging to user 1, not all rows; test_search_notes_none_user_id — call search_notes('', None) and assert it raises an exception or returns empty rather than all rows.

title: delete_note has no tests — silent exception suppression and SQL injection unverified
why: The function uses a bare except/pass block, meaning any DB error (constraint violation, connection failure, malformed note_id) is silently swallowed and the caller never knows. The f-string interpolation of note_id is also injectable. Without tests, neither the happy-path deletion nor the silent-failure branch is verified.
fix: test_delete_note_removes_row — insert a row, call delete_note(id), query the DB and assert the row is gone; test_delete_note_sql_injection — call delete_note("1 OR 1=1") and assert it raises or does not delete all rows; test_delete_note_nonexistent_id — assert no exception is raised but also that no rows are affected.

title: DELETE /notes/<id> route has no tests — admin gate and deletion response unverified
why: Without tests, there is no assertion that a request without X-Admin-Token returns 403, that a request with the correct token returns 204, or that the route actually invokes delete_note. A misconfigured gate would expose note deletion to any caller.
fix: test_remove_note_forbidden — DELETE /notes/1 without X-Admin-Token header and assert 403; test_remove_note_success — DELETE /notes/1 with correct X-Admin-Token header and assert 204 response and that the note is deleted.

title: POST /notes/filter route has no tests — eval-based RCE reachable with no guard
why: The route accepts a JSON body with an 'expression' key and passes it to applyFilterExpression which calls eval(). Without tests, there is no assertion that malicious expressions are blocked, that the 500 error path leaks a full traceback to the caller (it does — traceback.format_exc() is returned in the JSON response body), or that only the authenticated user's own notes are visible in the filter scope.
fix: test_filter_notes_rce_expression — POST {"expression": "__import__('os').getenv('HOME')"} and assert the response is not 200 or does not contain the env value; test_filter_notes_traceback_not_leaked — POST a bad expression and assert the 500 response does not include a 'trace' key with a server-side stack trace; test_filter_notes_valid_expression — POST a safe predicate and assert only matching notes are returned.

title: truncate long-text/ellipsis branch is untested
why: The existing test only covers the short-text (no-op) branch. The ellipsis branch — where text longer than 140 characters is cut and '...' appended — has no test. A regression that broke the truncation length or dropped the ellipsis would go undetected.
fix: test_truncate_long_text_appends_ellipsis — call truncate('a' * 200) and assert len(result) == 143 and result.endswith('...'); test_truncate_exact_boundary — call truncate('a' * 140) and assert the string is returned unchanged.
